      "title": "MetricAlertDetectorHandler is still abstract and cannot be instantiated",
      "body": "MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self), so any detector with this type will raise TypeError at runtime instead of returning a handler. Implement the required hooks, even as temporary stubs, or keep it subclassing DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation exists."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 222,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "get_state_data raises KeyError when a stateful detector has no counters",
      "body": "In StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data, counter_updates is initialized to {} and only populated if self.counter_names is truthy. The later construction of DetectorStateData unconditionally accesses counter_updates[gk]. If a subclass defines counter_names as an empty list, any call with non-empty group_keys raises KeyError. Initialize counter_updates to {gk: {} for gk in group_keys} or handle the no-counter case explicitly."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 327,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Redis state keys collide for None and empty-string group keys",
      "body": "build_dedupe_value_key, and similarly build_counter_value_key, converts a None group_key to an empty string before formatting the Redis key. A real group_key of '' therefore produces the same Redis key as None. Since DetectorState rows and fingerprints can distinguish None from '', dedupe values and counters can be shared or overwritten between these two group keys, causing skipped evaluations or wrong detector state. Use a distinct sentinel for None or otherwise namespace the keys."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py",
      "line": 244,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Tests do not verify the new occurrence hook receives correct inputs",
      "body": "build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts a value parameter but never uses it, and it returns fixed occurrence/event IDs. Several tests pass arguments that do not match the evaluated packet, such as building an expected occurrence with value 6 for a group whose packet value is 10, or building an occurrence for one group key while evaluating another. As a result, the tests would not catch regressions where build_occurrence_and_event_data receives the wrong group_key/value or produces non-unique occurrences. Make the mock incorporate group_key/value and fix the expected arguments."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",

      "body": "The evaluate method now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but its docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. Update the docstring to match the new return type so callers and implementers are not misled."
    }

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is still abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self), so any detector with this type will raise TypeError at runtime instead of returning a handler. Implement the required hooks, even as temporary stubs, or keep it subclassing DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation exists.

findings.title: get_state_data raises KeyError when a stateful detector has no counters
findings.body: In StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data, counter_updates is initialized to {} and only populated if self.counter_names is truthy. The later construction of DetectorStateData unconditionally accesses counter_updates[gk]. If a subclass defines counter_names as an empty list, any call with non-empty group_keys raises KeyError. Initialize counter_updates to {gk: {} for gk in group_keys} or handle the no-counter case explicitly.

findings.title: Redis state keys collide for None and empty-string group keys
findings.body: build_dedupe_value_key, and similarly build_counter_value_key, converts a None group_key to an empty string before formatting the Redis key. A real group_key of '' therefore produces the same Redis key as None. Since DetectorState rows and fingerprints can distinguish None from '', dedupe values and counters can be shared or overwritten between these two group keys, causing skipped evaluations or wrong detector state. Use a distinct sentinel for None or otherwise namespace the keys.

findings.title: Tests do not verify the new occurrence hook receives correct inputs
findings.body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts a value parameter but never uses it, and it returns fixed occurrence/event IDs. Several tests pass arguments that do not match the evaluated packet, such as building an expected occurrence with value 6 for a group whose packet value is 10, or building an occurrence for one group key while evaluating another. As a result, the tests would not catch regressions where build_occurrence_and_event_data receives the wrong group_key/value or produces non-unique occurrences. Make the mock incorporate group_key/value and fix the expected arguments.

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The evaluate method now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but its docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. Update the docstring to match the new return type so callers and implementers are not misled.
